scenes.say: Without Einstein, your GPS would drift about ten kilometers every day.
GPS works by timing signals from satellites, using super precise atomic clocks.
scenes.heading: HOW GPS WORKS

scenes.say: But the satellites move so fast that their clocks run slower, by about seven microseconds a day.
scenes.label: per day

scenes.say: And up there, gravity is weaker, which makes clocks run faster, by about forty-five microseconds.
scenes.label: per day

scenes.say: Together, the satellite clocks gain about thirty-eight millionths of a second, every day.
scenes.label: every single day

scenes.say: Sounds tiny. But the signals travel at the speed of light, so that adds up to around ten kilometers of error. Every day.
scenes.heading: SOUNDS TINY?

scenes.say: So engineers set the satellite clocks to tick slightly slower before launch. Einstein's theory, fixing your map every day.
scenes.heading: THE FIX

scenes.say: Did you know your phone needs relativity?
